aggregate.decomposition_convention: signed Sharpe change; negative values are decay; fee_decay includes deterministic fee and quoted-spread slippage
aggregate.finding: The strategy retained 7.2% of its screened risk-adjusted performance; the largest degradation came from counterfactual market stress.

design.causal_rule: signals use data through t and orders submit no earlier than t+1
design.world_source: deterministic synthetic generator; no external market data

decisions.reason: engine 'hftbacktest' is not allowed by this benchmark task

metric_definitions.fees: sum of native fill commissions in quote currency
metric_definitions.fill_ratio: orders with at least one native fill divided by submitted orders
metric_definitions.gross_return: ending marked equity before native fees divided by initial cash, minus one
metric_definitions.latency_cost: signed native fill cost relative to submission-time executable top of book in quote currency
metric_definitions.max_drawdown: maximum peak-to-trough decline of marked net equity
metric_definitions.net_return: ending marked equity after native fees divided by initial cash, minus one
metric_definitions.runtime_seconds: native adapter function wall-clock duration for this logical run; package import is reported in batch wall time
metric_definitions.sharpe: mean per-observation net equity return divided by population volatility, annualized by sqrt(252)
metric_definitions.slippage: signed native fill cost relative to submission-time mid in quote currency
metric_definitions.turnover: absolute native filled notional divided by initial cash

source_hash_convention: CRLF normalized to LF; all other source bytes preserved

strategy.execution_rule: signals use observations through t and submit at t+1; force flat at final observation
strategy.signal_rule: long when trailing fast mean is strictly greater than trailing slow mean; otherwise flat

task.objective: Measure how a fixed dual moving-average strategy degrades from analytical screening through certified event execution, deterministic costs, latency, and counterfactual market stress.
